newsitem.title: USA: Top Emerging market funds favor Russia, Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Top Emerging market funds favor Russia, Taiwan.

text.p: Four Russia funds and three Taiwan funds dominated top-ten rankings on over 1,400 emerging market funds surveyed over a three-month period, according to Micropal, which monitors emerging market funds.
The victory belt, however, goes to the Bangladesh Fund, which more than doubled in value over a three month period ending October 31, Micropal said.

The recent buying frenzy on the Dhaka Stock Exchange helped catapult the Bangladesh Fund, which is managed by Indosuez Asset Management Asia, to just over 128 percent for the time period surveyed, it said.
The Russia Value Fund LP ranked second place, up 59.86 percent, according to Micropal.

Rounding out the top five funds over three months was the Baltic Growth Fund, up 49.58 percent, Brunswick Russian Growth Fund, up 42.95 percent, and NatWest/IFC LAIF Venezuela Index Fund, up 36.14 percent, it said.
In Micropal's year-to-date rankings, the Korea Small Companies Trust surpassed all other funds, surging 171.71 percent in the first ten months of the year.

Trailing close behind was the Bangladesh Fund, up 144.64 percent, White Tiger Investment Co, up 125.99 percent, Blue Tiger Investment Co, up 119.83 percent, and Mercury ST Eastern European Fund, up 111.37 percent, said Micropal.
Micropal noted that the White and Blue Tiger funds invest in Russian equities, and the top ten for the period included four more Russian funds and an Eastern European equity fund.
"With only a few weeks left in 1996, the competition for the title of the best emerging market fund of 1996 is really heating up," said David Masters of Micropal.

"A few months ago, it appeared as though the Korea Small Companies Trust had the title all sewn up," he said. But "strong rallies in Russian and Bangladesh stocks have made the race a lot tighter," Masters added.
According to Micropal's figures, the Brazilian equity fund Patrmimonio New Fund Equity topped emerging market funds over the past three year period, with a gain of 155.01 percent.
JPBT Latin Fund, a regional equity fund, snatched the five-year spot by rising a stellar 1,026.95 percent. The New York-listed Chile Fund, up 546.28 percent, dominated the seven year rankings.
Finally, Capital International's Emerging Markets Growth Fund continued to lead all other funds in Micropal's 10-year rankings, with a total return of 951.03 percent for the period.
The survey uses U.S. dollar returns, net-asset-value to net-asset-value, and gross income is reinvested for the respective periods ending October 31, Mircopal said.
